topic: exact ordering-alias counterexample for systematic sibling resampling

public_evidence.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering
public_evidence.result: They give an explicit interleaved two-value counterexample where systematic resampling's conditional variance fails to decrease with particle count, while multinomial is O(1/n) and stratified/residual are still smaller. Both stratified and systematic are ordering-sensitive, but only systematic shares one offset across all strata.

derived_results.claim: Take even n particles ordered x1,x0,x1,x0,..., with total resampling mass omega on x1 and 1-omega on x0, 1/2<=omega<1, and f(x1)-f(x0)=1. Multinomial variance is omega(1-omega)/n. Stratified/residual variance is (2omega-1)(1-omega)/n. Systematic variance is (omega-1/2)(1-omega), independent of n. Thus systematic/multinomial variance ratio is n(omega-1/2)/omega and systematic/stratified ratio is exactly n/2 whenever omega>1/2.

At omega=0.75 and n=64, systematic variance is 0.0625, multinomial is 0.0029296875 and stratified is 0.001953125: systematic is 21.33x multinomial and 32x stratified. Increasing n worsens these ratios linearly because the systematic variance stays constant.

This is already a special case of the r121 architecture with q=W, so a systematic-resampling failure does not require exotic importance weights. In a semantic agent frontier, sorting/packing branches by score, source, class or prefix type can create periodic structure analogous to the interleaved comb; a single shared systematic offset can then synchronize offspring decisions across many strata.

Randomly permuting particles before systematic resampling can empirically destroy the adversarial ordering, as noted by Douc et al., but it adds a shuffle, changes reproducibility/locality and does not create a universal variance-dominance theorem. Independent stratified uniforms already provide the r120 one-step variance guarantee without requiring a random global reorder.

design_consequence.claim: Use independent stratified priority resampling as the default descendant allocator. If systematic resampling is introduced for speed, treat particle ordering as part of the algorithm state, run an ordering-alias diagnostic, and retain a stratified fallback. Never infer lower variance from the fact that systematic uses a stratified-looking grid.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The comb example is adversarial and does not imply systematic is usually bad; it shows lack of a robust variance guarantee.
Stratified resampling is itself ordering-sensitive in its exact distribution, although its conditional variance remains no larger than multinomial for a fixed ordering.
The counterexample concerns resampling variance, not estimator correctness when proper weights are used.
No real-agent or AGI capability conclusion follows.
next_tests: Build multi-generation semantic-tree simulations with score-sorted, alternating and randomly permuted orderings; compare stratified/systematic/iid normalizing-constant variance and genealogy diversity.
Measure cache/locality cost of independent stratification versus systematic on realistic batched agent rollouts before choosing an implementation default.
Combine r121 recursive weights and r122 ordering diagnostics in one auditable resampler interface that logs q, ordering transform, resampling scheme and expected counts.
